newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says competition easier than fcast.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says competition easier than fcast.

text.p: The world's largest digital mobile phone producer Nokia Oy said on Tuesday the impact of competition and price erosion in the first quarter of the year had been smaller than it expected.
"We saw some competition but the impact was less than we expected," Pekka Ala-Pietila, head of the cellular phone arm Nokia Mobile Phones, told a telephone conference.

Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila said earlier he expected price erosion for the whole year to be 15-20 percent, which Nokia could manage. Nokia would continue to maintain market share in "the very tough competitive mobile phone market," he said.
Asked why competition did not show more in margins, Ala-Pietila said the mobile phone market was very difficult and that it required high technology as well as mastering large volumes.
"There are now more cellular phones producers than personal computers," he said.
The number of competitors had remained at around 60 since the early 1990s, but some had left the market and others entered, probably going only for certain segments, he said.
"Adding value in all segments is the key in this business," he added.
Ollila earlier said Nokia had suucceeded during Q1 to reach its 10 percent target margin in mobile phone sales.
